stemMd: A bacterial population contains a few antibiotic-resistant variants before treatment. After treatment, resistant cells dominate. Which explanation best fits natural selection?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The antibiotic deliberately instructs every cell to adapt.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The treatment changes every bacterial species into a virus.

options.label: C
options.textMd: All cells must acquire identical mutations at the same moment.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Susceptible cells die more often, so pre-existing resistant variants leave more descendants.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Resistance proves that bacteria never mutate.

explanationMd: The treatment changes relative survival and reproduction. Variants already able to resist it become more frequent; the environmental challenge selects among variants rather than planning a useful mutation.

distractorRationale.a: Selection does not require directed instruction.
distractorRationale.e: Mutation is one source of variation.
distractorRationale.b: Selection does not transform bacteria into viruses.
distractorRationale.c: Pre-existing variation already explains the result.
